newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha holds, LSWR bullish after spot deal.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha holds, LSWR bullish after spot deal.

text.p: Naphtha prices were little changed in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday, while sentiment in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market turned bullish after a spot deal was fixed at a 55-cent premium, traders said.
A South Korean firm was said to have bought about 400,000 barrels of Indonesian LSWR at around 55 cents over the Pertamina formula.
This compares with premium levels of 20 to 30 cents in May amid ample supplies caused by an accidental closure of a hydrocracker at Indonesia's Dumai refinery.

As Pertamina's allocation for July lifting is likely to be as small as three million barrels due to maintenance closures at some refineries in Indonesia, market sentiment is expected to remain bullish for the time being, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August was assessed at $204.00/205.00 per tonne. On Tuesday, it was traded once at $205.00, and twice at $204.00.

In naphtha term talks in London, KPC's initial offer price was $20 over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes, traders said. Most potential buyers have not yet indicated their bidding levels, they said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
